body.objective: Students will be able to name environmental problems.
successCriteria: I can name environmental problems in Spanish
I can describe causes and consequences
I can connect problems to places in the Spanish-speaking world
body.hook: The Amazon rainforest, which crosses several Spanish-speaking countries, the glaciers of Patagonia and the coral reefs of the Caribbean are among the world's most important ecosystems, and they're under pressure.

study.title: Nuestro planeta
study.question: What environmental problems affect the Spanish-speaking world and ours?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud, written for this lesson):
El medio ambiente tiene muchos problemas. La deforestación en la selva amazónica destruye el hábitat de muchos animales. La contaminación del aire es un problema grave en las ciudades grandes. Por el cambio climático, los glaciares de la Patagonia y de los Andes se derriten. Hay mucha basura de plástico en los océanos. Algunas especies, como el jaguar, están en peligro de extinción. En Canadá también tenemos problemas: los incendios forestales y la contaminación del agua.
Cause and consequence: por + noun (because of): Por la contaminación, el aire está sucio. causa (causes): La deforestación causa inundaciones. por eso (that's why).
Activity: groups receive a map with problem icons (Amazonía, Ciudad de México, Patagonia, el Caribe, Alberta) and write one cause-and-consequence sentence for each.
study.source: Original text written for this lesson.
steps: Use por, causa and por eso
discussion: Which animal in the text is endangered?
study.product: Write six cause-and-consequence sentences about environmental problems in the Spanish-speaking world and Canada.

body.objective: Students will be able to give opinions and suggestions.
body.iCan: I can give opinions and suggestions.
successCriteria: I can give opinions with en mi opinión, creo que and pienso que

body.hook: "En mi opinión, debemos reciclar más." "Es importante usar menos plástico." Giving opinions and suggestions is how people work together on environmental solutions, in any language.

vocabulary.definition: I believe that / I think that

study.title: ¿Qué debemos hacer?
study.question: How do I give opinions and suggestions about the environment?
study.passage:
Toolkit (written for this lesson):
Opinions: En mi opinión, … / Creo que… / Pienso que… / Para mí, …
Suggestions: Debemos usar el transporte público. Tenemos que reciclar. Es importante ahorrar agua. Es necesario plantar árboles. No debemos usar bolsas de plástico.
Agreeing and disagreeing: Estoy de acuerdo. / No estoy de acuerdo porque… / Tienes razón, pero…
Debate statements: 1. Las escuelas deben prohibir las botellas de plástico. 2. Es mejor ir a la escuela en bicicleta o a pie. 3. Todos debemos comer menos carne.
Structure: opinion + reason + example: Creo que las escuelas deben prohibir las botellas de plástico porque producen mucha basura. Por ejemplo, en nuestra cafetería hay muchas botellas en la basura.
Activity: four corners (muy de acuerdo, de acuerdo, en desacuerdo, muy en desacuerdo); each corner prepares two arguments in Spanish and debates politely.
study.source: Original statements and activity written for this lesson.
discussion: Which statement did you feel strongest about?
How did you support your opinion?
study.product: Write an opinion paragraph on one debate statement with your opinion, two reasons, an example and two suggestions.

body.objective: Students will be able to explore environmental efforts in Spanish-speaking countries.
body.iCan: I can explore environmental efforts in Spanish-speaking countries.
successCriteria: I can describe environmental efforts in Spanish-speaking countries
I can explain what we can learn from them
I can present an environmental success story in Spanish
body.hook: Costa Rica generates almost all of its electricity from renewable sources. Ecuador's constitution gives rights to nature itself. Spanish-speaking countries are leaders in some of the world's most creative environmental efforts.

study.title: Ejemplos verdes
study.question: What environmental efforts are happening in the Spanish-speaking world?
study.passage:
Success stories (written for this lesson from public sources):
Costa Rica: for several years it has generated almost all its electricity from renewable sources such as hydroelectric, geothermal, wind and solar power. A large share of the country is protected in national parks and reserves, and ecotourism is an important industry.
Ecuador: its 2008 constitution recognized the rights of nature (los derechos de la naturaleza). The Galápagos Islands became a national park in 1959 and are protected for their unique species.
México: the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve in Michoacán protects forests where millions of monarch butterflies spend the winter after migrating from Canada and the United States; it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Chile: large new national parks in Patagonia were created in partnership with conservation donors.
Sentences: Costa Rica usa energía renovable. Ecuador protege los derechos de la naturaleza. Las mariposas monarca viajan desde Canadá hasta México.
Connection to Canada: monarch butterflies also live in Canada in summer, so protecting them requires cooperation between countries.
Activity: groups research one success story and present it in Spanish: ¿Dónde? ¿Qué hacen? ¿Por qué es importante? ¿Qué podemos aprender?
study.source: Summary from public sources including UNESCO and national park agencies.
discussion: How does Costa Rica produce electricity?
How do monarch butterflies connect Canada and Mexico?
study.product: Present an environmental success story from a Spanish-speaking country in Spanish, explaining what it is, why it matters and what we can learn.
